title: Add a committed, reproducible GenerateData benchmark harness for the TSK-0008 perf gate
description:
## Summary

The TSK-0008 performance gate (parent) requires that coarse-resolution / extraction changes do not materially regress preview generation. Reproduced numbers exist in records (VPU10 total ~204ms; VPU16 total ~626ms median GC-clean; VPU16 extraction-only 133.5ms) but there is NO committed, reproducible benchmark harness in-repo that runs GenerateData at those VPUs and reports the per-stage timings on demand. Runtime already has timing instrumentation (GenerationDiagnostics per-stage timings, CreatureMeshGenerator.GenerateData, MarchingCubesExtractor stage stopwatches, editor timing report). This task adds a committed harness so the perf gate is actually verifiable in-repo and future perf-gated work (e.g. TSK-0129) can benchmark before/after.

## Scope
- Add a benchmark harness (Unity-runnable on demand) that, for one representative creature fixture at VPU 10 and VPU 16, runs CreatureMeshGenerator.GenerateData over N reps and reports per-stage timings (FieldSampling, MeshActiveCellConstruction, contour/extraction, total) with median + allocation handling (GC-clean where possible).
- Reuse existing instrumentation and the GenerationDiagnostics path. No production behavior change.
- Record expected baselines from the TSK-0008 records but treat timing as environment-sensitive: assert a generous regression ceiling / ratio rather than a brittle hard ms cutoff, OR make the timing run opt-in (not part of the default green suite) to avoid flakiness. Keep the default Runtime PlayMode suite green and non-flaky.
- Document the exact command/filter/menu item to run it and where to record results.
- Add at least one before/after sanity fixture path so a future change can compare.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One committed harness reproduces GenerateData total + sub-stage timings at VPU10/VPU16 on demand with recorded methodology (reps, median, GC handling).
- Default Runtime PlayMode suite stays green and non-flaky (no timing test added to the always-run set unless it asserts only a very generous ceiling).
- No production behavior change; deterministic extraction/topology unaffected.
- README/validation note documents the run command and result location.

## Validation
- dotnet build Runtime + Tests.Runtime clean.
- Unity: run the harness; record VPU10/VPU16 total + sub-stage numbers and methodology. Run the default Runtime PlayMode suite and confirm no new failures/regressions.
- git diff --check clean.

## Blockers
None.

## Next Step
Design the harness to reuse GenerationDiagnostics + CreatureMeshGenerator.GenerateData, choose fixture + VPUs, implement as opt-in/lenient, validate, and document.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
ROUND 1 (BeastMaster) implementation evidence.

Added a committed, on-demand GenerateData benchmark harness (test-infra only; NO production change):
- Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/GenerateDataBenchmark.cs (+ Unity-generated .meta)
- Assets/Scripts/README.md: concise note (how to run, result location, reference baselines).

Design decisions (see report):
1) Opt-in, not in the default suite: the harness class has NO [Test]/[UnityTest] methods, so Unity never auto-discovers it and the always-run Runtime PlayMode suite is unchanged and cannot flake on timing. It is invoked explicitly (Unity MCP execute_code / editor call): GenerateDataBenchmark.Run() (default VPU 10+16, 7 timed reps + 1 warmup per VPU).
2) Reuses the existing instrumentation: each rep calls CreatureMeshGenerator.GenerateData(definition, diagnostics) and reads GenerationDiagnostics per-stage timings (SdfCompile, FieldSampling, MeshExtraction, and sub-stages ActiveCellConstruction/ContourResolution) + TotalTime. No timing asserts anywhere; no flake risk.
3) Fixture: deterministic self-contained multi-part creature (torso body spline + fused head/tail/4 legs/2 eyes spheres), built fresh per VPU via BuildFixture(voxelsPerUnit); watertight at both VPUs. Follows the committed CC-091 body-spline + spherical-decoration authoring pattern (no limb-chain machinery), so it is robustly valid. No existing committed dino-like fixture exists in tests to reuse (the authored dino JSON is a concurrent uncommitted workstream file, intentionally not referenced).
4) GC methodology: +1 warmup discarded; GC.Collect+WaitForPendingFinalizers once before timed reps; median guards occasional GC stalls; 'min' reported as the GC-clean proxy. Managed alloc/rep via Profiler.GetTotalAllocatedMemoryLong deltas; methodology states native/Burst/Unity-object allocations are outside the managed heap and are not captured.

comments.body:
ROUND 1 (BeastMaster) validation evidence.

Validation gate (all passed):
- git diff --check: clean (exit 0). Only new files: Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/GenerateDataBenchmark.cs (+ .meta) and the Assets/Scripts/README.md note. No production file touched. All modified/untracked Data/Tasks/*.json, docs/audits/*.md, and Assets/Creatures/dinus_uprightus.json belong to the concurrent animation workstream and were left untouched.
- dotnet build --no-restore: ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj clean (0 warnings/0 errors); ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj clean.
- Unity harness run (MCP execute_code, Editor, Unity 6000.5.9f1), 7 timed reps + 1 warmup per VPU:
  VPU 10: grid 80x80x80, samples 531441; 6600 tris / 3302 verts, watertight=True; total median 97.5 ms, min 92.8 ms; SdfCompile 0.1; FieldSampling 28.3 (min 26.0); MeshExtraction 37.4 (min 34.4); ActiveCellConstruction 8.0; ContourResolution 19.0; managed alloc/rep median 2.2 KiB.
  VPU 16: grid 128x128x128, samples 2146689; 16330 tris / 8167 verts, watertight=True; total median 215.7 ms, min 208.0 ms; FieldSampling 50.2 (min 48.7); MeshExtraction 115.7 (min 113.9); ActiveCellConstruction 40.0; ContourResolution 53.0; managed alloc/rep median 2.2 KiB.
- Default Runtime PlayMode suite: 526/526 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (same total as before this round -> harness adds no auto-run tests; no regression).

Methodology recorded in the report header and Assets/Scripts/README.md.

Note: these numbers are on the new harness fixture, NOT the TSK-0008 creature. TSK-0008's gate numbers (VPU10 ~204ms; VPU16 ~626ms GC-clean) were measured on a different creature and remain the gate reference. This harness gives a committed, reproducible before/after path for future perf-gated work on a stable fixture.

Did NOT commit or push (orchestrator owns commit).
